newsitem.title: ITALY: Klein, Karan are U.S. pioneers at Milan shows.
newsitem.headline: Klein, Karan are U.S. pioneers at Milan shows.

text.p: U.S. fashion designers are retaliating against Italian rivals and their campaigns across the Atlantic, with Calvin Klein and Donna Karan set to grace Milan catwalks with their menswear collections.

Curtain-up for the mens' ready-to-wear autumn/winter 1996/97 is Sunday, with the first fashion statement coming from top Italian designer Gianni Versace, who recently dressed Madonna for the London premiere of the movie musical Evita.
Among the big Italian names of Giorgio Armani, Gianfranco Ferre, Dolce & Gabbana and Gucci billed for the five-day event, more and more foreign names are visible.
Germany's Jil Sander and Britain's Vivienne Westwood and Katharine Hamnett have thrown down the gauntlet to their Italian competitors in shows past and will be present again this season.

But Karan is breaking new ground. Patti Cohen, senior vice president of corporate communications at Karan's New York office, told Reuters by telephone this was the first time the U.S. stylist had shown in Milan. Karan has sold outside America virtually since her first women's collection in 1985.
Karan has been designing collections for men since 1991 and Cohen said as the company expanded internationally, showing in Milan furthered the group's business and creative interests.
"It benefits our European customers and we have been bringing the line there to sell. Plus all the American buyers are there anyway so it's really a perfect fit," she said.

On a personal level, it was the designer's dream to present a collection in Milan. "Donna has said that to her Milan is the heart and soul of menswear. The tailors, the fabric mills and the factories are the best in the world and she's relied on them from the day we started the company," Cohen said.
Both Karan and Klein feature on Wednesday, the penultimate day of the shows.
Klein, who displayed a jeans line here last March, is presenting his second line here for the first time -- the cK Calvin Klein designs for younger buyers which will be shown off on the catwalk.

In the last few months, Italian designers have swelled their ranks considerably in the United States, with Versace, Armani and others opening new boutiques in New York and some previewing latest designs for their second line collections in the city.
For Milan, Monday is a key day in the shows, with Krizia, whose real name is Mariuccia Mandelli, Ferre and fashion duo Dolce & Gabbana all sending out their line-ups.
Fashion house Fendi features on Tuesday along with successful design team Gucci and a presentation by Prada, another stylist who has homed in on the U.S. market.
Thursday sees Briton Katharine Hamnett and the end of the shows is punctuated as usual that evening by Armani.
